rationale: All four lenses ran clean and parseable, acceptance found zero failing criteria (24/24 pass, spec present), and verification-gap reported no gaps; the one blocking item is the standards audit's commit-format violation (two unticketed commit subjects) which is unambiguous to fix. Three findings (no ownership/visibility scoping on the clone source lookup, an unfiltered-is_active source lookup, and a check-then-insert duplicate-name race) are genuine but pre-existing — all three reproduce patterns already present in create()/get_by_id() elsewhere in this service, outside this story's scope — and are recorded in code-review-deferred.md. Six additional lens items were dismissed as noise or below the blocking-severity floor: suggested-name staleness (an explicitly documented design tradeoff), a redundant categories length validator, a unicode/byte truncation edge case in clone_naming.py (reused verbatim per the story), a double authenticate dependency declaration (an existing, harmless project-wide pattern), an O(n) copy-number scan only material at ~10^6 copies, and an empty-source-name truncation edge case.

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description' for repository commits; two subjects in range use 'clone-mcp-full-copy-remove-stripping: add planning artifacts' and 'clone-mcp-capability: add planning artifacts', neither ticket-prefixed

New source files and new test files all carry the Apache 2.0 header; naming allocation is extracted into its own module (service/mcp/clone_naming.py) rather than appended inline despite mcp_config_service.py being 835 lines; new code uses 'str | None' unions, parameterized generics and 'from __future__ import annotations' per the types guide

New endpoints both depend on authenticate + admin_access_only matching the central auth pattern; clone_from_form copies is_system/is_public only from the source model, never from the request body; clone_naming.allocate_name builds its LIKE query through SQLModel's parameterized select with an escaped pattern and a strict regex, no string-built SQL; no credentials or secrets are logged

findings.file: commit history (2 commits in review range)
findings.title: Commit subjects missing EPMCDME ticket prefix
findings.problem: git-workflow.md's Commit Message Format section requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; two commit subjects in the review range — 'clone-mcp-full-copy-remove-stripping: add planning artifacts' and 'clone-mcp-capability: add planning artifacts' — omit the ticket prefix entirely.
findings.impact: A documented commit-format rule is a blocking standard per the review gate; the subjects also don't tie back to EPMCDME-15538 for traceability.
findings.recommendation: Reword the two subjects to lead with the EPMCDME-15538 ticket prefix (e.g. 'EPMCDME-15538: Add planning artifacts for ...'), via rebase/reword if the branch is not yet merged.
